skip_reason: Not a sales call. This is an outbound service-recovery / follow-up call to an existing customer (Edwina Reyes) about negative GatherUp feedback on a completed 8/15 move. Entire call is damage triage (dresser leg, bookshelf, bed frame), a claims handoff, mover coaching, and an offered $100 goodwill check. No quote, no pricing, no booking — the sales scorecard does not apply.
top_strength: Strong service-recovery instincts: Dustin took clear ownership, pushed back on a make-shift fix in favor of a professional furniture-repair vendor, and proactively offered a $100 goodwill check without the customer asking. He also closed the loop on the coaching side, telling her the newer mover had already been coached on the specific behaviors she described.
coaching_note: Not gradeable on the sales rubric. One process note for the claims side: Dustin twice mixed up the two movers' names (referred to 'Tyler' when the customer's concern was about Gavin, and vice versa) while explaining who had been coached — on a recovery call that undercuts the credibility of the fix. Confirm names against the job record before the call.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and non-defensive — repeated affirmations ('Absolutely, no, I appreciate that information'), genuine ownership language, and the customer ended up joking with him and declining the compensation because she felt bad, which is a clear rapport signal.
